title: WAL components and data flow
caption: A backend writes records into WAL buffers and then pg_wal on disk, and the same WAL feeds crash recovery and replicas.

badges.meaning: The backend builds a WAL record with XLogInsert
The record bytes are copied into WAL buffers in shared memory
WAL is flushed to the segment files in pg_wal

title: INSERT and COMMIT through WAL
caption: At COMMIT only the WAL is forced to disk, and the dirty data page is written later by a checkpoint.

badges.meaning: Client sends INSERT to its backend
Backend changes the page in shared buffers, which becomes dirty
Backend writes the change record into WAL buffers
Backend adds the commit record to WAL buffers
XLogFlush writes and syncs WAL to pg_wal
Backend tells the client the commit is done
Later, a checkpoint writes the dirty page to the data files

title: Anatomy of a WAL record
caption: Zoom from a 16MB segment file to an 8kB page, to one record, to the 24 byte XLogRecord header fields.

badges.meaning: A WAL segment file in pg_wal is a run of 8kB pages
Each page has a page header followed by WAL records
A record is a header, block headers, main data header, then block and main data
The XLogRecord header fields, including xl_rmid which names the owner of the redo code
